n: Isaiah summons all nations and the whole earth to listen. Chapters 34 and 35 form a pair: judgment on the wicked world, then joy for the redeemed.

f.w: Come near, ye nations, to hear

n: The Lord is angry with all nations and their armies; He has devoted them to destruction and handed them over to slaughter.

f.g: Hebrew ḥerem — devoted completely to destruction.

n: Their dead will lie unburied, the stench will rise, and the mountains will flow with their blood. The imagery is meant to shock, showing the seriousness of rebellion against God.
The stars will dissolve and the sky roll up like a scroll; the heavenly bodies will fall like withered leaves. Latter-day scripture uses this imagery for the Second Coming.

f.w: the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll

n: God’s sword, prepared in heaven, comes down in judgment on Edom (Idumea), the people He has condemned. In latter-day revelation Idumea stands for the wicked world.

f.g: The Greek name for Edom, Israel’s neighbor and long-time enemy.

n: The Lord’s sword drips with blood and fat like a sacrificial knife. He holds a “sacrifice” in Bozrah, Edom’s capital — a grim image of judgment.

f.g: Parts offered on the altar in sacrifices (Leviticus 3:4).

n: Wild oxen, bulls, and steers will fall with them — the powerful leaders of the nation. The land will be soaked with blood.

f.g: Wild oxen — not the mythical one-horned creature.

n: It is the Lord’s day of vengeance, a year of repayment to defend Zion’s cause. God will set right the wrongs done to His people.

f.w: the day of the LORD's vengeance

n: Edom’s streams will turn to tar, its soil to burning sulfur, and its land to blazing pitch — like Sodom’s destruction.
The fire will burn day and night, its smoke rising forever. The land will lie desolate for generations, and no one will travel through it.

f.w: the smoke thereof shall go up for ever

n: Desert birds and wild animals will take over. God will measure Edom with the line of chaos and the plumb line of emptiness — undoing creation.

f.g: A desert bird, perhaps a pelican or owl.

n: Its nobles will have no kingdom to rule, and all its princes will vanish.
Thorns will grow in its palaces and nettles in its fortresses. It will become a haunt for jackals and a home for owls.
Desert creatures and hyenas will meet there; wild goats will call to each other; night creatures will settle there to rest.

f.g: Wild goat, or goat-demon of folklore.

n: Owls will nest and raise young there, and vultures will gather in pairs. Edom becomes home only to wild birds.

f.g: Perhaps an arrow-snake or owl; uncertain.

n: Search the Lord’s book and read: none of these creatures will be missing, each with its mate, because the Lord commanded it and His Spirit gathered them. His word is completely reliable.

f.w: no one of these shall fail

n: God has assigned the land to them by lot and measured it out with His line. They will possess it forever — a solemn reversal of how Israel once received its inheritance.

f.w: he hath cast the lot for them
